translationRepairs: On leaving the purple he was made Secretariat Gentleman of Liang and promoted to groom of the heir apparent.
On doffing coarse cloth he was made Secretariat Gentleman of Liang and promoted to groom of the heir apparent.
解褐 is the formula for doffing coarse cloth to take office; “leaving the purple” invents 紫 and mistranslates 褐.
When Emperor Wen governed Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the firm-resolution establishment and soon promoted him to left chief secretary of the secretariat.
When Emperor Wen governed Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the firm-resolution establishment and soon promoted him to left chief secretary of the Minister of Education.
司徒左長史 is left chief secretary under the Minister of Education (司徒), not under the secretariat; 司空 would be Minister of Works.
When Emperor Wen was interior administrator of Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the Firm Resolution establishment and promoted him to left chief secretary of the Secretariat.
When Emperor Wen was interior administrator of Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the Firm Resolution establishment and promoted him to left chief secretary of the Minister of Education.
Same office string 司徒左長史; replacing Secretariat with Minister of Education restores the Three Dukes title.

At that time Emperor Wu sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with gifts. Chang had Zai draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and the text needed no correction. Huang reported this to Emperor Wu, and Zai was soon summoned as compiler-historian.

At that time Emperor Wen sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with gifts. Chang had Zai draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and the text needed no correction. Huang reported this to Emperor Wen, and Zai was soon summoned as compiler-historian.
時世祖使…言之世祖 names Shizu; in Chen that is Emperor Wen, while Emperor Wu is 高祖.

At that time Emperor Wu sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with various goods; Chang entrusted Zai to draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and fluent and the text needed no correction; when Huang returned he reported this to Emperor Wu, and soon Zai was summoned as compiler-historian.

At that time Emperor Wen sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with various goods; Chang entrusted Zai to draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and fluent and the text needed no correction; when Huang returned he reported this to Emperor Wen, and soon Zai was summoned as compiler-historian.
Both 世祖 mentions in the sentence are Emperor Wen of Chen, not Emperor Wu.
Collation variant: city, the prince served as inspector of Yangzhou, [2] and Gu Yewang and Wang Bao of Langye were both his retainers; the prince greatly prized their gifts.
The Prince of Xuancheng was inspector of Yangzhou; [2] Gu Yewang and Wang Bao of Langye both served as his retainers, and the prince greatly valued their talents.
Collation across 宣／（成）／城王 yields 宣城王; Wikisource corrects 宣（成）〔城〕王, and 才 is talents, not gifts.

The imperial edict has already soared into the vast sky, [5] yet the apprehensive still peek into marshes seeking it.
The jiaoming bird has already soared into the boundless sky, [5] yet the hunter still searches the marshes for it.
Wikisource corrects 鷦（鵬）〔敕〕 to the jiaoming bird; 虞者 is a hunter, so “imperial edict” and “apprehensive” are false.
imperial edict has already soared into the vast sky, [5] yet the lookout still peeks into marshes seeking it.
The jiaoming bird has already soared into the vast sky, [5] yet the hunter still peers into the marshes in search of it.
Same 鷦敕／虞者 correction as r0008; the literal subject is the bird, not an edict, and the seeker is a hunter.

At the time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong; his family for generations were farmers—to Hua alone he loved learning, associated with gentlemen and scholars, and broadly read the classics and histories, skilled at composition.

At the time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong; his family for generations were farmers—Hua alone loved learning, associated with gentlemen and scholars, and broadly read the classics and histories, skilled at composition.
至華獨好學 means Hua alone loved learning; “to Hua alone he loved learning” invents a second subject and breaks the grammar.
The end does not contend, [6] which is the truth of things.
Root and branch do not contend, [6] which is the true nature of things.
Collation 本／（來）／末 is corrected to 本末; Wikisource and the following 本之與末 confirm root-and-branch, not “the end” alone.
